Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act empowers the government to grant exemptions from customs duties in the public interest.
This SRO is issued under the authority of this section to provide specific duty concessions for the development of the tourism industry.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides the legal basis for granting exemptions on value added tax and supplementary duty.
National Board of Revenue: The government issues this order in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Tourism Industry Equipment: The order grants partial exemption from customs duties, regulatory duties, value added tax, and supplementary duties on specific items imported for the construction of high-quality hotels to promote the tourism industry.
The exemption applies to imports exceeding five percent value-based customs duty, provided that such goods are not already covered by the scope of S.R.O. 157-AIN/2012.
S.R.O. 157-AIN/2012: This existing notification serves as the reference point for items already receiving duty exemptions, which are excluded from the scope of this new order.

Customs Duty Concession: The duty concession under this notification is restricted to goods used in the construction of residential hotels that hold international hotel franchise status or are designated as high-quality hotels by the relevant civil aviation and tourism ministry.
In the event of any discrepancy between the tariff classification code and the product description within the provided schedule, the product description shall prevail.

Value Added Tax: Applicants operating as residential hotels are required to be registered for the purpose of the Value Added Tax.

National Board of Revenue: Hotel authorities must submit an application along with specific documents to the National Board of Revenue to obtain duty concession facilities.
Value Added Tax: Applicants are required to submit copies of their business registration and tax certificates to qualify for specific benefits.
Bangladesh Investment Development Author: A copy of the registration certificate issued by the investment board is a mandatory document for the application process.
Hotel Management: Hotel authorities must provide documentation, including building layout plans and a detailed list of imported goods with their corresponding commodity codes, to support their application. International chain hotels are exempt from certain certification requirements if they provide proof of their franchise agreement.
Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism: The Ministry is responsible for forming a verification committee comprising stakeholders and experts to set international quality standards for hotels. Based on these standards, the Ministry issues the necessary certificates of compliance.
